source.display_title: 05/29/2026 - Eric Bergman x Andrew Musial  — Lost

prospect.name: Kurt Kelsey
prospect.occupation: Sales; works from home, roughly 9 to 7, mostly seated at a sit-stand desk on calls, travels for work 1-3 times a month
prospect.family_status: Married to Christy; planning to try for children from around the end of 2026; one dog
prospect.training_background: Trains 3x/week at a group fitness gym (Hyrox-style, barbells, kettlebells, conditioning) in the mornings; previously trained at a primal-movement gym in Denver 2019-2021 and felt stronger then; stopped entirely for roughly a year after moving to Florida, back training for about 18 months; recently broke a 200 lb bench press; eats mostly whole-food, low-carb, no seed oils; uses hotel gyms when travelling

signals: Self-directed and already training effectively; 'my status quo currently isn't terrible. I feel like I am working out.'
Anchored hard to a functioning cheap alternative: '$160 bucks a month' group gym, and expected coaching to be 'like $1,000 for six months'
Asked repeatedly for a reduced-scope, programming-only product rather than the full service
Not price-resistant out of incapacity — 'Not necessarily' when asked if he lacked the cash — but out of value comparison against competing spend

goals.text: Age gracefully and avoid the CrossFit road where joints break down
Get stronger, especially chest, and maintain a strong physique he is happy to be shirtless in year-round in Florida
Be as strong as possible before the baby arrives so that fitness is easier to maintain through parenthood
A training approach that survives travel and missed classes so nothing falls off the wagon
Move like he did at the primal-movement gym — functional single-leg and flow work rather than movements 'you would never actually do in real life'

pains.text: The gym has become so popular he is waitlisted out of morning classes and cannot reliably get in
Travel once to three times a month drops him from three sessions to one or two
Stopped training entirely for about a year after moving; named it himself as an accountability problem, 'I honestly think it was just more of like an accountability issue'
Feels he should be seeing more results for the work he is putting in; chest has always lagged
Current gym programmes movements he does not see as transferable to real life; feels he has more muscle but is less strong than in 2019-2021
Sits roughly ten hours a day on calls with only calf raises to break it up

objections.raw_quote: Because six grand, even for six months, that's $1,000 a month, basically.
objections.rep_response: Reframed away from a per-month comparison — 'you're not buying a gym membership, you're buying a transformation right now' — without re-establishing any cost of inaction.

objections.raw_quote: if there is a package that like doesn't. Include, you know, meal planning, for example, or like 24-7 concierge service ... here's like three months worth of workouts prescribed for different weights and, you know, go nuts
objections.rep_response: Did not offer a tier; instead introduced a $1,200 30-day trial, and only after the prospect had closed the door surfaced Primal University at $200/month.

objections.raw_quote: there's just other expenses and priorities that are getting in the way at this point, namely, like, my addition on the house
objections.rep_response: Asked whether the cash was actually absent, then suggested putting it on a credit card for the points; did not run the not-the-right-time play.

objections.raw_quote: I don't think I'm going to do it for six grand for six months.
objections.rep_response: Isolated finances ('is there anything else that would be stopping you'), then offered to break the payment up; prospect answered that the total is the total.

tiers.note: Primal University Skool community, $200 per month, cancel any time — a separate product surfaced as a downsell

prospect_financials.note: Declined to say he lacked the cash — 'Not necessarily' — and cited a house addition as the competing priority; currently pays about $160/month for his gym

evidence: 'I don't think I'm going to do it for six grand for six months.'
'at least it's a no for right now'
Declined the $1,200 trial too: 'I'm probably going to have to go figure something else out, at least for the near term.'

Counter-evidence: he stayed warm and asked to be sent the Primal University information — 'that might be something of interest' — and said he might revisit after the house addition, so a future low-ticket sale is live
No payment taken, no link sent, no follow-up call booked
outcome.next_step: Rep to email Primal University ($200/month) details and follow up after the prospect's summer and house addition

notable.note: The Drive title names 'Eric Bergman' but the prospect on the recording is Kurt Kelsey throughout. Rep improvised a $1,200 30-day trial that is not part of the stated offer, and when that failed suggested the prospect put the spend on a credit card 'for those points' immediately after the prospect had described a competing house-addition budget. The consequence frame was never run, so the price landed with no cost of inaction behind it — the prospect's own position was that his status quo is fine.

quality.notes: Substantial and sustained label inversion: long stretches of rep discovery questions are attributed to Kurt Kelsey and prospect answers to the rep, most heavily between 00:02:00-00:12:00 and again around 00:17:00-00:19:30 and 00:39:44-00:40:12. Role was read from content throughout. The rep is also labelled 'Andrew Jin (Primal Instinct)' while the folder and batch record say Andrew Musial.
